output.short_explanation: The /apply form renders only email, amount, term, income and the auto route checkbox; the accepted payload is allowlisted to those keys, persistence writes only those fields into a schema with no hobby column, and onward payloads are limited to email/amount/term and email/amount/income. No purposeless field is collected, accepted, persisted or forwarded.
output.detailed_explanation:
Code facts: The customer dashboard builds the application form at views.py 0031-0032 from inputbox("Contact email","email"), inputbox("Requested amount (EUR)","amount"), select("Term in months","term",[6,12,24,36]), select("Income band","income",["low","medium","high"]) and a single checkbox name="auto" value="yes"; no other applicant attribute is rendered. The POST body is parsed at app.py 0053-0055 into data (max_num_fields=18, duplicate keys rejected) and dispatched at app.py 0083-0084 to store.submit. store.py 0067 enforces require(set(data) <= {"email","amount","term","income","auto"},"Unexpected application field."), so a key such as "hobby" is refused before any write. The cases schema at store.py 0036-0038 has columns email, amount, term, income, confirmed, route, stage, restricted and no free-form or hobby column; the INSERT at store.py 0077-0078 writes owner, officer, email, amount, term, income, route, stage, and the summary title at store.py 0079 is derived from amount and term. Onward payloads: offer() at store.py 0111-0112 returns case id, email, amount, term; portable() at store.py 0114-0116 returns email, amount, income; transfer at store.py 0201-0203 stores only that portable payload in receiver.payload.

Requirement: Article 5(1)(c) as scoped here requires that the application form and the accepted /apply payload — including what is persisted or sent onward — be limited to the applicant inputs necessary for the stated purposes: contact email for delivery, amount and term for the requested offer, income band for assessment. The scenario stipulates that a hobby has no business purpose in this fixture, so any collection, acceptance, persistence or forwarding of a hobby field would be an in-scope counterexample. The trigger is present: the scenario describes an actual application submission through this form and payload path.

Justification: Each stage of the data path is bounded to the necessary set. The form offers no hobby-type field (views.py 0031-0032); the server-side allowlist rejects any unexpected key (store.py 0067), so a hobby value cannot enter the accepted payload; persistence targets a schema without such a column and writes only the necessary attributes plus the route/stage bookkeeping (store.py 0036-0038, 0077-0079); and onward sends carry only email/amount/term (offer) and email/amount/income (portable/transfer) (store.py 0111-0116, 0201-0203). The "auto" checkbox is a processing-route selection (automatic vs manual review, store.py 0075) tied to the notice's automatic-decision option, not an additional applicant attribute, so it does not create a minimization defect. No supported in-scope counterexample appears in the supplied artifacts, and no decisive unresolved dependency remains within the named behavior; the verdict is therefore SUPPORTED for this scoped obligation only.

evidence.explanation: Customer /apply form renders only email, amount, term, income and the 'auto' route checkbox; no hobby or other purposeless field is offered.
POST body parsed into data with bounded field count and duplicate rejection; no extra fields synthesized.
/apply forwards the parsed payload to store.submit, the sole application collection sink.
Allowlist set(data) <= {email, amount, term, income, auto} rejects any unexpected key such as 'hobby'.
cases schema has no hobby column; only email, amount, term, income, route, stage etc. can be persisted.
INSERT persists only email, amount, term, income, route, stage; summary title derived from amount and term.
Onward payloads limited: offer() sends email/amount/term; portable() sends email/amount/income.
Transfer stores only the portable payload (email, amount, income) for the receiving controller.
